dedupe_keys.name: awsm snowmelt water supply modelling workflow

description: The Automated Water Supply Model is a Python workflow developed by the US Department of Agriculture's Agricultural Research Service for snow-fed basin forecasts. It distributes weather-station data with SMRF, runs the iSnobal snow energy and mass balance model, and processes results through a repeatable configuration. Users provide stations, terrain, snow and basin parameters plus forecast dates; outputs are distributed snow and water-supply estimates over those basins. The model resolution and period are user-configured, not a fixed national grid. The source is public domain in the United States and explicitly dedicated CC0 worldwide in its licence file, with documentation and stable release v0.10 available free. A limitation is that the main branch is experimental and may not work with the full modelling system; reuse should target the tested release for operational comparison. Local mountain forcing and snow observations still govern forecast quality. AWSM supports reservoir inflow and drought planning. The catalogue's model-raven is a separate catchment model for comparison; no direct linkage was tested. No installer or forcing data was downloaded.
